1: # RoundZero – Product Specification
2: 
3: ## 0. Overview
4: 
5: RoundZero is a hiring platform that is being built in two layers:
6: 
7: 1. **Core hiring platform**
8:    - company profiles
9:    - public jobs board
10:    - candidate profiles
11:    - one-click apply
12:    - applicant review workflow
13: 
14: 2. **AI interview and evaluation layer**
15:    - async structured interviews
16:    - multi-pass candidate evaluation
17:    - explainable reports
18:    - ranked candidate recommendations
19: 
20: The product is not meant to be “just another jobs board.” The end state is a system where companies do less manual screening because candidates arrive already evaluated. But the current build priority is to make the non-AI platform solid first, so the AI layer lands on top of a complete hiring workflow instead of compensating for product gaps.
21: 
22: ### Core Value Proposition
23: 
24: > “Post jobs, collect structured candidate profiles, and replace first-round screening with explainable AI interviews.”
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## 1. Product Position
29: 
30: ### 1.1 What RoundZero Is
31: 
32: - A role-specific hiring platform for companies and candidates
33: - A structured application funnel
34: - A future AI-driven first-round interview layer
35: - A candidate evaluation and decision-support system
36: 
37: ### 1.2 What RoundZero Is Not
38: 
39: - Not a generic social network for jobs
40: - Not a resume dump with no downstream workflow
41: - Not a black-box ranking system with unexplained outputs
42: - Not a video-interview platform
43: 
44: ### 1.3 Current Product State
45: 
46: Today, the app is primarily the **core platform layer**:
47: 
48: - public marketing landing page
49: - public company directory
50: - public jobs board
51: - role-specific login and onboarding
52: - company job management
53: - candidate profile/settings
54: - one-click apply
55: - applicant review pages and status tracking
56: - in-app workflow notifications
57: 
58: The AI interview, evaluation, report, and ranking systems are now live.
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 2. Core Principles
63: 
64: ### 2.1 Solid Platform Before AI
65: 
66: The AI layer should not be used to paper over missing product fundamentals. The non-AI hiring workflow must be credible on its own first.
67: 
68: ### 2.2 Explainability Over Black Box
69: 
70: When the AI layer is added, every recommendation must be evidence-backed and legible to hiring teams.
71: 
72: ### 2.3 Structured Inputs Beat Shallow Filtering
73: 
74: The platform should gather cleaner, more useful candidate and job data than a typical job board. Candidate profiles, resumes, work history, skills, and application state should all be structured enough to support later evaluation.
75: 
76: ### 2.4 Async by Default
77: 
78: The product should minimize scheduling friction. Applications, profile setup, future interviews, and notifications should all fit asynchronous workflows.
79: 
80: ### 2.5 Opinionated, Not Over-Abstracted
81: 
82: RoundZero should choose a clear hiring workflow instead of becoming an infinitely configurable ATS.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 3. Users
87: 
88: ### 3.1 Candidates
89: 
90: Candidates use RoundZero to:
91: 
92: - create a profile
93: - upload a resume
94: - browse public jobs
95: - apply with one click
96: - track application status
97: - later complete AI interviews
98: 
99: ### 3.2 Companies
100: 
101: Companies use RoundZero to:
102: 
103: - create a company profile
104: - post and manage jobs
105: - review applicants
106: - track application pipeline state
107: - later review AI interview reports and rankings
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ## 4. Current Core Product
112: 
113: ### 4.1 Candidate Experience
114: 
115: Current candidate flow:
116: 
117: 1. Visit marketing site, jobs board, or company page
118: 2. Sign in via candidate login
119: 3. Complete onboarding:
120:    - name
121:    - headline
122:    - resume upload
123: 4. Maintain profile in settings:
124:    - bio
125:    - skills
126:    - work history
127:    - links
128:    - resume
129: 5. Browse jobs
130: 6. Apply with one click
131: 7. Track applications in dashboard
132: 
133: Key rules:
134: 
135: - applying requires a profile resume
136: - applications snapshot the current profile state needed for review
137: - candidates should not re-enter redundant links or resume info per application
138: 
139: ### 4.2 Company Experience
140: 
141: Current company flow:
142: 
143: 1. Sign in via company login
144: 2. Complete onboarding:
145:    - name
146:    - short description
147:    - industry
148:    - size
149: 3. Maintain full company profile in settings
150: 4. Create jobs
151: 5. Manage open/draft/archived jobs
152: 6. View applicants per job
153: 7. Review applicants on dedicated applicant detail pages
154: 8. Update application statuses
155: 
156: ### 4.3 Public Experience
157: 
158: Public users can:
159: 
160: - view the landing page
161: - browse companies
162: - view company pages
163: - browse jobs
164: - view job detail pages
165: 
166: This matters because RoundZero is both:
167: 
168: - a workflow application for signed-in users
169: - a discoverable public hiring surface
170: 
171: ---
172: 
173: ## 5. Core Product Gaps (Resolved)
174: 
175: The platform-hardening priorities listed below were completed before the AI layer went live:
176: 
177: ### 5.1 Candidate Post-Apply Polish
178: 
179: - [x] Empty states and guidance on application tracking surfaces
180: - [x] Clear next-step communication after status changes
181: - [x] Interview card on application detail with CTA and status
182: 
183: ### 5.2 Company Workflow Quality
184: 
185: - [x] Pipeline summary cues (applicant count, evaluated count)
186: - [x] Real report scores and recommendation badges on applicant list
187: - [x] Full report timeline on applicant detail
188: 
189: ### 5.3 Notifications Delivery Layer
190: 
191: - [x] In-app notifications as canonical record
192: - [x] Resend email delivery for `report_ready` and `interview_expired`
193: - [x] Delivery tracking on notification rows
194: 
195: ### 5.4 Public Route Cleanup
196: 
197: - [x] Expired-job-specific public error UI
198: - [x] Dead CTA branches removed from public job detail
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ## 6. AI Layer (Live)
203: 
204: RoundZero now includes the AI hiring layer on top of the solid platform.
205: 
206: ### 6.1 AI Interview Mode
207: 
208: - in-app async chat (text-based, no video)
209: - preserves context and supports adaptive follow-ups
210: - works across time zones without scheduling friction
211: 
212: ### 6.2 AI Interview Goals
213: 
214: The AI interview:
215: 
216: - validates resume claims
217: - probes role-relevant knowledge
218: - evaluates communication quality
219: - detects inconsistency or vagueness
220: - gathers evidence for structured evaluation
221: 
222: ### 6.3 Evaluation Goals
223: 
224: The evaluation layer:
225: 
226: - scores communication, problem solving, ownership, and role fit
227: - generates an explainable report with strengths, weaknesses, insights, and evidence
228: - produces a recommendation (strong yes / yes / lean no / no)
229: - flags contradictions via deterministic fallback when LLM output is invalid
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: ## 7. High-Level Product Flow
234: 
235: ### 7.1 Current Platform Flow
236: 
237: ```
238: Company creates profile → Company posts job → Candidate creates profile →
239: Candidate uploads resume → Candidate applies → Company reviews applicant →
240: Company updates status
241: ```
242: 
243: ### 7.2 AI-Enabled Flow
244: 
245: ```
246: Company posts job → Candidate applies → AI interview →
247: Evaluation pipeline → Candidate report → Ranking →
248: Company reviews top candidates
249: ```
250: 
251: ---
252: 
253: ## 8. Candidate Data Model (Product-Level)
254: 
255: Candidate profile should contain:
256: 
257: - name
258: - headline
259: - resume reference
260: - bio
261: - skills
262: - work history
263: - external links
264: 
265: Application should contain:
266: 
267: - job
268: - candidate
269: - apply-time resume snapshot
270: - apply-time profile metadata snapshot
271: - application status
272: 
273: This separation matters:
274: 
275: - the candidate profile is the source of truth
276: - the application is a snapshot of what was submitted at that time
277: 
278: ---
279: 
280: ## 9. Company Data Model (Product-Level)
281: 
282: Company profile should contain:
283: 
284: - name
285: - slug/public URL
286: - description
287: - logo
288: - website
289: - industry
290: - size
291: - founded year
292: - location
293: - tech stack
294: - culture/perks
295: - social links
296: 
297: Job should contain:
298: 
299: - title
300: - description
301: - requirements
302: - location
303: - type
304: - experience level
305: - salary info
306: - team size
307: - headcount
308: - expiry info
309: - status
310: 
311: ---
312: 
313: ## 10. AI Report Structure (Live)
314: 
315: The candidate report is the main AI output artifact.
316: 
317: Live sections:
318: 
319: - candidate header (name, job, apply date)
320: - summary
321: - recommendation badge (strong yes / yes / lean no / no)
322: - overall score (0–100)
323: - dimension scores (communication, problem solving, ownership, role fit)
324: - strengths
325: - weaknesses
326: - insights
327: - evidence
328: - pre-screening to interview to post-evaluation timeline
329: - interview transcript (substantive messages only)
330: 
331: The report is readable by a hiring manager without requiring trust in a hidden scoring system.
332: 
333: ---
334: 
335: ## 11. Company Workflow Goals
336: 
337: Before AI:
338: 
339: - jobs are easy to post and manage
340: - applicants are easy to review
341: - pipeline status is understandable
342: - resume/profile data is accessible
343: 
344: After AI (live):
345: 
346: - companies review structured reports instead of raw first-round resumes
347: - candidate ranking is explainable and scored
348: - teams can move faster without losing trust
349: - evaluated candidates are ranked by overall score on the job applicants page
350: 
351: ---
352: 
353: ## 12. Candidate Workflow Goals
354: 
355: Before AI:
356: 
357: - profile setup is fast
358: - resume upload is simple
359: - applying is low-friction
360: - application tracking is clear
361: 
362: After AI:
363: 
364: - interviews are async and not exhausting
365: - candidates understand where they are in the process
366: - the experience still feels fair and role-relevant
367: 
368: ---
369: 
370: ## 13. Notifications and Communication
371: 
372: RoundZero will need transactional communication for key workflow events.
373: 
374: Current and planned uses:
375: 
376: - application submitted confirmations
377: - application status updates
378: - company-facing applicant activity notifications
379: - interview-ready notifications later
380: 
381: Recommended provider for email delivery:
382: 
383: - **Resend** for transactional email
384: 
385: Why:
386: 
387: - simple developer experience
388: - good fit for app-triggered transactional messages
389: - enough for MVP without building a complex email system
390: 
391: ---
392: 
393: ## 14. Success Criteria
394: 
395: ### 14.1 Before AI
396: 
397: The core platform is successful when:
398: 
399: - a candidate can create a profile, upload a resume, apply, and track progress without confusion
400: - a company can create a job, receive applicants, review resumes/profile snapshots, and manage statuses reliably
401: - the hiring workflow feels coherent without any AI magic
402: 
403: ### 14.2 After AI
404: 
405: The AI layer is successful when companies say:
406: 
407: > “I would move these candidates forward without manually screening them first.”
408: 
409: or
410: 
411: > “This saves us real hiring time.”
412: 
413: ---
414: 
415: ## 15. AI Layer Product Decisions
416: 
417: The following decisions are required **before Phase 4 (AI Interview)** begins. These define how the AI layer integrates with the existing platform.
418: 
419: ### 15.1 Decision 1: Application Status Lifecycle
420: 
421: **Question:** How do we model application statuses when the AI layer introduces new evaluation stages?
422: 
423: **Current State:**
424: - `applications.status` uses: `applied`, `interviewing`, `evaluated`, `rejected`
425: - AI-LAYER.md suggests: `applied`, `pre_screening`, `interview_invited`, `interview_in_progress`, `evaluated`, `shortlisted`, `rejected`
426: 
427: **Decision:** **Extend the existing `applications.status` enum to include all 8 statuses**
428: 
429: **Rationale:**
430: - Simpler query patterns (single status column)
431: - Clear audit trail of all state transitions
432: - No schema duplication or hidden parallel state machines
433: - Status transitions follow the funnel: `applied` → `pre_screening` → (`interview_invited` | other outcome) → `interview_in_progress` → `evaluated` → (`shortlisted` | `rejected`)
434: 
435: **Transition Rules:**
436: - Only companies can move `evaluated` → `shortlisted` or `rejected`
437: - The system auto-advances through `pre_screening` → `interview_invited` → `interview_in_progress` → `evaluated`
438: - A company can manually reject at any pre-evaluation stage
439: - When a job's `final_report_target` is reached, the system stops advancing new candidates out of `pre_screening`
440: 
441: **Implementation:**
442: - Update `enums.ts`: extend `applicationStatusSchema` to include all 8 statuses
443: - Update `APPLICATION_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` to enforce the funnel order
444: - Update all client-facing status labels to distinguish internal (pre-evaluation) vs. external (candidate-visible) states
445: 
446: ---
447: 
448: ### 15.2 Decision 2: Candidate-Facing Messaging After Apply
449: 
450: **Question:** What messaging do candidates see at each evaluation stage?
451: 
452: **Decision: Hide pre-evaluation stages from candidates**
453: 
454: **Candidate-Visible Status Mapping:**
455: - `applied` / `pre_screening` → "Application Received"
456: - `interview_invited` → "Interview Ready"
457: - `interview_in_progress` → "Interview in Progress"
458: - `evaluated` → "Under Review"
459: - `shortlisted` → "Shortlisted"
460: - `rejected` → "Not Moving Forward"
461: 
462: **Candidate Messages:**
463: - Strong fit: "Zero invited you to complete an interview for this role."
464: - Medium fit: "Zero has a few additional questions to help evaluate your fit."
465: - Low fit: "Application received and under review."
466: 
467: **Implementation:**
468: - Add `getVisibleApplicationStatus()` helper for status mapping
469: - Add `applicationStatusCandidateLabelMap` in `config.ts` for exact copy
470: - Update candidate dashboard to use visible status only
471: 
472: ---
473: 
474: ### 15.3 Decision 3: Medium-Fit Follow-Up Medium
475: 
476: **Question:** Where and how do medium-fit candidates answer clarifying questions?
477: 
478: **Decision: Use synchronous chat UI (same as full interview)**
479: 
480: **Rationale:**
481: - Preserves interview context and adaptability
482: - Candidates get dynamic follow-ups based on answers
483: - Lower barrier to answer 2–3 questions than to do a full interview
484: - Reuses the same agent and transcript infrastructure
485: 
486: **Implementation:**
487: - Medium-fit candidates are invited to a "quick evaluation" via the interview chat UI
488: - Agent system prompt is modified to ask 2–3 clarifying questions instead of full interview script
489: - Questions adapt based on resume gaps identified in pre-evaluation
490: - Output is still a structured report, same as full interview
491: - Same `interviews` table is used; a `metadata` field can flag it as "quick_eval"
492: 
493: ---
494: 
495: ### 15.4 Decision 4: Company View With and Without AI Reports
496: 
497: **Question:** Can companies see (and act on) applications before AI evaluation completes?
498: 
499: **Decision: Companies see full pipeline, but pre-evaluation candidates are read-only**
500: 
501: **Before AI Evaluation Completes:**
502: - Raw applicant list with resume, profile snapshot
503: - Status badge: "Application Received" or "Under Review"
504: - No scoring or evaluation report yet
505: - Cannot change status (read-only until evaluation completes)
506: 
507: **After AI Evaluation Completes:**
508: - Same applicant list, now includes:
509:   - AI evaluation report (summary, scores, strengths, concerns)
510:   - Can change status or shortlist/reject
511: 
512: **Quota-Exhausted State:**
513: - Once `final_report_target` reports are generated, new applicants remain in pre-evaluation
514: - Companies still see them in the pending list with full profile data
515: - No new AI reports are generated until the company increases the limit (future feature)
516: 
517: **Minimum Viable Company View:**
518: | State | Shows | Actions |
519: |---|---|---|
520: | Pre-evaluation | Name, resume, date, status | None |
521: | Post-evaluation | Above + AI score, summary, recommendations | Shortlist / Reject |
522: | Quota exhausted | Same as pre-evaluation | Manual review / reject only |
523: 
524: **Implementation:**
525: - `getApplicationReviewById` returns profile + evaluation report (if it exists)
526: - UI conditionally renders "evaluation in progress" vs. full report view
527: - Action buttons only appear post-evaluation
528: 
529: ---
530: 
531: ### 15.5 Decision 5: Pre-Evaluation Output Format Validation
532: 
533: **Question:** Is the pre-evaluation output (score + missing requirements + confidence + next step) sufficient?
534: 
535: **Current Spec:**
536: - **Score:** 0–100 (overall fit)
537: - **Missing Requirements:** List of role requirements not met
538: - **Confidence:** High/Medium/Low
539: - **Next Step:** "Invite to RoundZero" | "Ask follow-ups" | "Hold / Reject"
540: 
541: **Validation Plan:**
542: 
543: 1. Run 5–10 real applications through manual evaluation using this format
544: 2. Get hiring manager feedback:
545:    - Would you trust this to decide "invite" vs. "ask follow-ups"?
546:    - Are missing requirements useful, or want different dimensions?
547:    - Should confidence be visible to company or internal only?
548:    - Is 0–100 score clear, or prefer tier (Strong/Medium/Low)?
549: 3. Adjust output based on feedback
550: 4. Document final schema in `AI-LAYER.md`
551: 
552: **Validation Status:**
553: - Pre-evaluation pipeline is live and producing scores
554: - Pre-evaluation only decides "invite to full interview" vs. "not yet"
555: - It does NOT rank candidates or make final hiring decisions
556: - If confidence is low, default to "ask follow-ups" rather than reject
557: - Real-world validation with hiring managers remains pending (deferred to post-MVP)
558: 
559: ---
560: 
561: ### 15.6 Decision 6: Final Report Target
562: 
563: **Question:** How many final reports should RoundZero deliver per job, and what happens when that target is reached?
564: 
565: **Decision:** Each job has a `final_report_target` (default: 5, max: 15). The system should deliver that many final reports whenever enough eligible candidates exist.
566: 
567: This target is based on completed reports, not interview invites.
568: 
569: **Rationale:**
570: - Prevents evaluation noise for roles with only 1–2 openings
571: - Keeps costs predictable for companies
572: - Forces selectivity in the funnel
573: - Default of 5 is small enough to review quickly but large enough to find strong matches
574: 
575: **When Target Is Reached:**
576: - The system stops creating new interviews for that job
577: - Remaining pending candidates stay in `pre_screening` (NOT auto-rejected)
578: - Candidates receive a `position_filled` notification: "This position has received enough evaluations. Your application is still on file and the company may review it directly."
579: - Companies still see unevaluated applicants in a read-only pending list and can manually reject them
580: 
581: **Interview Slot Policy:**
582: - Every invite has a 48-hour expiry window
583: - If a candidate does not complete in time, interview status becomes `expired`
584: - Candidates can cancel interviews voluntarily; status becomes `cancelled`
585: - Expired/cancelled slots are recycled to the next best eligible candidate
586: - Capacity is computed as:
587:   - `remainingReports = final_report_target - completedReports`
588:   - `availableInviteSlots = remainingReports - activeInterviews(status IN pending|in_progress)`
589: 
590: **Implementation:**
591: - Add `final_report_target INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5` to `jobs` table (max: 15)
592: - Add field to job creation/edit form with copy: "How many final candidate reports should RoundZero deliver for this role? (Max 15)"
593: - Enforce max 15 in Zod schema and server functions
594: - Pre-evaluation + lifecycle manager computes invite capacity from report completion and active interviews
595: - Background workflow and cron lifecycle manager send `position_filled` when target is reached
596: 
597: ---
598: 
599: ## 16. One-Line Definition
600: 
601: > “A hiring platform that starts with a solid async application workflow and evolves into an explainable AI-driven first-round interview and candidate evaluation system.”

(End of file - total 601 lines)
</content>

1: # RoundZero – Architecture
2: 
3: ## 0. Status
4: 
5: This document reflects the app as it transitions from **platform-only** to **platform + AI layer**.
6: 
7: **Currently live:**
8: 
9: - TanStack Start application (Nitro runtime)
10: - Postgres-backed hiring platform
11: - role-based company/candidate workflows
12: - public company and jobs browsing
13: - one-click applications with profile snapshots
14: - durable in-app notifications with Resend email delivery
15: - Cloudflare Workflows for pre-evaluation and post-evaluation pipelines
16: - Cloudflare Agents SDK interview runtime (`AIChatAgent`)
17: - AI-driven candidate evaluation and structured reports
18: - `final_report_target` quota system per job
19: - 8-status application lifecycle with pre-screening funnel
20: - dedicated candidate interview workspace at `/interview/$interviewId`
21: - company-facing report views with scoring and timeline
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 1. Stack
26: 
27: | Layer | Technology |
28: | --- | --- |
29: | Framework | TanStack Start (React 19, Vite 7) |
30: | Runtime (app) | TanStack Start + Nitro |
31: | Runtime (AI) | Cloudflare Workers (separate edge Worker with Workflows + Durable Objects) |
32: | Database | Postgres (Docker locally, Neon intended for prod) |
33: | Typed queries | SQLC |
34: | Migrations | dbmate |
35: | Auth | Google OAuth with server-side cookie session |
36: | UI | shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS v4, Hugeicons |
37: | Validation | Zod |
38: | Notifications | In-app inbox + Resend email delivery |
39: | File storage | Cloudflare R2 for resumes and company logos |
40: | AI layer | Cloudflare Workers AI + edge Worker |
41: | AI pipelines | Cloudflare Workflows (durable multi-step) in edge Worker |
42: | Interview runtime | Cloudflare Agents SDK (`AIChatAgent`) + `workers-ai-provider` |
43: | Chat transport | WebSocket via Agents SDK (streaming) |
44: | Linting | Biome |
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: ## 2. Runtime Architecture
49: 
50: ### Main App (Nitro)
51: 
52: The app runs as a standard TanStack Start app with server functions for:
53: 
54: - auth
55: - jobs
56: - applications
57: - company profile management
58: - candidate profile management
59: - dashboard metrics
60: - notifications
61: - resume/logo storage contracts
62: 
63: ### AI Edge Worker (Cloudflare Workers)
64: 
65: The AI layer lives in a separate `edge/` directory as a standalone Cloudflare Worker:
66: 
67: - Hono HTTP server with `/pre-evaluate`, `/post-evaluate`, and internal report endpoints
68: - Cloudflare Workflows run pre-evaluation and report generation pipelines
69: - Agents SDK routes interview agents over WebSocket/HTTP
70: - R2 stores resumes
71: - Workers AI binding provides model inference
72: 
73: **Why a separate Worker:**
74: - Cloudflare Workflows only execute in `wrangler dev` / deployed Workers, not in the Vite plugin's local dev
75: - The main app needs fast HMR and standard Node.js dev (Nitro)
76: - The edge Worker gets real workflow step execution, bindings, and Durable Objects
77: - One command (`bun run dev`) starts both via `bun run --parallel`
78: 
79: **Communication:**
80: - Main app calls edge Worker via authenticated HTTP `fetch()`
81: - Edge Worker reads/writes the same Postgres database
82: - Both share DB schema and SQLC-generated queries (generated to both locations)
83: 
84: ### Directory Layout
85: 
86: ```
87: roundzero/              # Main app - TanStack Start + Nitro
88: ├── app/                # Routes, components, server functions
89: ├── db/                 # Migrations, seed
90: └── package.json        # TanStack Start deps
91:

203: ## 5. Directory Structure
204: 
205: ```
206: app/
207: ├── routes/              # TanStack file-based routes
208: ├── features/            # Product feature modules
209: ├── components/          # Shared/global UI
210: ├── shared/              # DB, middleware, form helpers, shared utilities
211: ├── lib/                 # Small app utilities

215: edge/
216: ├── src/
217: │   ├── index.ts         # Worker entrypoint (Hono HTTP server)
218: │   ├── workflows/       # Cloudflare Workflow classes
219: │   ├── agents/          # Durable Object agent classes

221: │   └── shared/          # DB connection, env validation

230: Conventions:
231: 
232: - feature-first structure
233: - SQL lives beside each feature under `queries/queries.sql`
234: - generated SQLC output is the typed query boundary
235: - server functions are the app-facing mutation/read boundary

237: ---
238: 
239: ## 6. Database Schema
240: 
241: Source of truth:
242: 
243: - `db/migrations/20260328081657_init.sql`
244: 
245: Schema dump:
246: 
247: - `db/schema.sql`
248: 
249: ### Key Tables
250: 
251: #### `users`
252: 
253: - identity
254: - Google auth linkage
255: - app role (`company` or `candidate`)
256: 
257: #### `companies`
258: 
259: - owned by a company user
260: - contains both onboarding data and public profile data
261: - includes public `slug`
262: 
263: #### `candidate_profiles`
264: 
265: - one per candidate user
266: - stores:
267:   - headline
268:   - `resume_key`
269:   - bio
270:   - skills
271:   - work history
272:   - links
273: 
274: #### `jobs`
275: 
276: - owned by a company
277: - stores structured hiring data
278: - includes:
279:   - status
280:   - salary info
281:   - team/headcount
282:   - `final_report_target` (default 5, max 15) — controls how many final reports companies receive
283:   - `interview_questions` (JSONB, for AI agent context)
284:   - `expires_at`
285:   - `archived_at`
286: 
287: #### `applications`
288: 
289: - unique per `(job_id, candidate_id)`
290: - stores:
291:   - `resume_key` snapshot
292:   - `metadata` snapshot for non-resume candidate profile data
293:   - status: `applied`, `pre_screening`, `interview_invited`, `interview_in_progress`, `evaluated`, `shortlisted`, `rejected`
294: 
295: This is important architecturally:
296: 
297: - `candidate_profiles` is the current source of truth
298: - `applications` is the apply-time snapshot
299: 
300: #### `pre_evaluations`
301: 
302: - one per application
303: - stores lightweight pre-evaluation output:
304:   - `score` (0–100)
305:   - `missing_requirements` (JSONB)
306:   - `confidence` (high/medium/low)
307:   - `next_step` (invite_roundzero / ask_followups / hold)
308: 
309: #### `interviews`
310: 
311: - link between applications and AI interview sessions
312: - stores:
313:   - `type`: `'full'` | `'quick_eval'`
314:   - `status`: `'pending'` | `'in_progress'` | `'completed'` | `'expired'` | `'cancelled'`
315:   - `metadata` (JSONB) — includes `expiresAt`, `expiredAt`, `cancelledAt`, `cancellationReason`
316:   - `started_at`, `completed_at`
317: 
318: #### `reports`
319: 
320: - evaluation output after interview completion
321: - stores structured report data:
322:   - overall score, recommendation
323:   - dimension scores (technical, communication, experience relevance)
324:   - strengths, concerns, evidence
325:   - question/answer timeline
326: 
327: Quota semantics:
328: 
329: - `final_report_target` is consumed by completed reports, not interview invites
330: - invite capacity per job is computed as:
331:   - `remainingReports = final_report_target - completedReports`
332:   - `availableInviteSlots = remainingReports - activeInterviews(status IN pending|in_progress)`
333: - if an interview expires or is cancelled, that slot is recycled and the next best candidate is invited
334: 
335: ### Schema Decisions
336: 
337: - No DB enums/check constraints for app-domain statuses
338: - Zod validates enum-like values in app code
339: - No triggers
340: - `updated_at` is set explicitly in update queries
341: - JSONB is used for structured but flexible data
342: - all FKs use `ON DELETE RESTRICT`
343: 
344: ---
345: 
346: ## 7. Query and Type Strategy
347: 
348: - SQLC is the typed DB layer
349: - generated `queries_sql.ts` files are never hand-edited
350: - no manual DB/data-shape types should be re-declared in app components when they can be inferred from SQLC or server function return types
351: - JSONB columns should be passed as raw JS objects/arrays, not stringified
352: 
353: Data flow pattern:
354: 
355: 1. SQL query in `queries.sql`
356: 2. SQLC generates typed query function
357: 3. feature server function wraps query and business rules
358: 4. route loader or mutation consumes server function
359: 5. components infer types from loader/server return values
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ## 8. Auth Architecture
364: 
365: Current auth flow:
366: 
367: 1. Candidate or company hits a role-specific login route
368: 2. Google OAuth succeeds
369: 3. server upserts the user
370: 4. session cookie is written
371: 5. role determines onboarding/dashboard path
372: 
373: Characteristics:
374: 
375: - simple and sufficient for current phase
376: - cookie-session based
377: - no DB-backed session table
378: 
379: Future note:
380: 
381: - Better Auth remains a later optional migration if more auth methods are needed
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## 9. Current Application Flow
386: 
387: ### Candidate profile + resume
388: 
389: Current intended flow:
390: 
391: 1. Candidate completes onboarding
392: 2. Candidate uploads resume through the app
393: 3. app stores `resume_key` on `candidate_profiles`
394: 4. candidate can maintain profile in settings
395: 
396: ### Applying
397: 
398: 1. Candidate selects a job
399: 2. app checks if they already applied
400: 3. app checks whether `candidate_profiles.resume_key` exists
401: 4. app creates application row
402: 5. application snapshots:
403:    - `resume_key`
404:    - profile metadata
405: 
406: ### Company review
407: 
408: 1. Company views a job or the dedicated applicants page for that job
409: 2. navigates into a dedicated applicant/application detail route
410: 3. sees submitted resume, snapshot data, timestamps, and current status
411: 4. updates application status from that review surface
412: 
413: ---
414: 
415: ## 10. Resume Storage Architecture
416: 
417: Resume handling uses a **contract-first** design.
418: 
419: ### Current model
420: 
421: - the database stores `resume_key`, not `resume_url`
422: - onboarding/settings use file-picking UI
423: - the server already exposes resume upload/read boundaries
424: - resume uploads now use real Cloudflare R2 signed URLs in the current runtime
425: 
426: ### Resume server boundaries
427: 
428: Current candidate resume server functions:
429: 
430: - `createResumeUploadTarget`
431: - `finalizeResumeUpload`
432: - `getResumeDownloadUrl`
433: 
434: Current company/application resume server function:
435: 
436: - `getApplicationResumeDownloadUrl`
437: 
438: ### Current flow
439: 
440: 1. client requests signed upload target
441: 2. server creates user-scoped key:
442:    - `resumes/<userId>/<uuid>--<sanitized-file-name>.<ext>`
443: 3. client uploads directly to Cloudflare R2
444: 4. server verifies the object exists in R2 during finalize
445: 5. server stores `resume_key` on `candidate_profiles`
446: 6. candidate self-view and company applicant review use short-lived signed URLs
447: 
448: ### Runtime note
449: 
450: - Resume upload uses S3-compatible R2 API from the main app server with presigned `PUT`/`GET` URLs
451: - The edge Worker accesses the same R2 bucket via native `env.RESUMES` binding for workflow resume extraction
452: 
453: Why `resume_key` instead of `resume_url`:
454: 
455: - stable internal reference
456: - avoids coupling DB state to delivery URL format
457: - easier to move between CDN/signed URL strategies later
458: 
459: ---
460: 
461: ## 11. Notifications Architecture
462: 
463: Notifications are implemented as a durable in-app inbox with Resend-backed email delivery as a secondary best-effort channel. In-app notification records are the primary system of record.
464: 
465: ### Current model
466: 
467: - `notifications` table stores:
468:   - `id`
469:   - `user_id`
470:   - `type`
471:   - `payload`
472:   - `read_at`
473:   - `email_delivery_status`
474:   - `email_delivery_error`
475:   - `email_delivery_attempted_at`
476:   - `email_delivery_sent_at`
477:   - `email_provider_message_id`
478:   - `created_at`
479: - supported event types:
480:   - `application_status_changed`
481:   - `report_ready`
482:   - `interview_invited`
483:   - `interview_expired`
484:   - `position_filled`
485:   - `job_published`, `job_archived`, `job_closed`
486:   - `application_withdrawn`
487: - application statuses include all 8: `applied`, `pre_screening`, `interview_invited`, `interview_in_progress`, `evaluated`, `shortlisted`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`
488: - the app shell/dashboard header renders the inbox surface
489: 
490: ### Current module layout
491: 
492: ```
493: app/features/notifications/
494: ├── components/
495: │   ├── notification-email-template.tsx
496: │   └── notification-inbox.tsx
497: ├── config.ts
498: ├── queries/
499: │   ├── queries.sql
500: │   └── queries_sql.ts
501: ├── server/
502: │   └── functions.ts
503: └── services/
504:     └── email.ts
505: ```
506: 
507: Provider:
508: 
509: - **Resend**
510: 
511: Current email-backed use cases:
512: 
513: - candidate application status updates
514: - company-side report ready notifications
515: - interview expiry notifications
516: 
517: Future email-backed use cases:
518: 
519: - interview ready / interview reminder
520: - position filled notifications
521: 
522: Recommended architecture:
523: 
524: - write a notification record to the database first
525: - treat in-app notifications as the primary system of record
526: - send email as a secondary best-effort delivery channel for selected events
527: - keep notification sending behind server-side functions/services
528: - trigger notifications from explicit workflow events, not UI-only actions
529: - persist delivery result directly on the notification row while there is only one secondary transport
530: - do not couple domain logic directly to a provider SDK in routes/components
531: 
532: Current delivery tracking:
533: 
534: - `notifications`
535:   - keeps `type` + `payload` as the canonical event record
536:   - stores email delivery attempt/result fields directly on the row
537: 
538: Future extension points:
539: 
540: - move email delivery attempts into a separate table once we need retries, webhooks, or multiple secondary channels
541: 
542: Design principle:
543: 
544: - if email delivery fails, the notification still exists in-app
545: - email is a transport, not the canonical event record
546: 
547: Current module additions:
548: 
549: - `app/features/notifications/services/email.ts`
550: 
551: ---
552: 
553: ## 12. Job Lifecycle Architecture
554: 
555: Jobs support:
556: 
557: - draft/open/closed states
558: - archive behavior
559: - `expires_at` with date picker on create/edit
560: - stale role indicator (90+ days with no expiry)
561: - auto-close on read for expired jobs
562: - hidden-by-default expired/closed jobs on public surfaces
563: - `interview_questions` JSONB field for future AI agent context
564: 
565: AI integration:
566: 
567: - `final_report_target` controls how many final reports companies receive per job
568: - `interview_questions` (JSONB) feeds into agent system prompts
569: 
570: ---
571: 
572: ## 13. Testing Architecture
573: 
574: Two Postgres containers:
575: 
576: | Container | Port | Purpose |
577: | --- | --- | --- |
578: | `rz_pg_dev` | 6311 | development |
579: | `rz_pg_test` | 6312 | tests |
580: 
581: Testing approach:
582: 
583: - real Postgres for query and workflow tests
584: - no DB mocking for query/business-logic layers
585: - shared test setup handles cleanup
586: - seed helpers create minimal valid records
587: 
588: Current coverage focus:
589: 
590: - auth queries
591: - companies queries
592: - jobs queries/business logic
593: - applications queries/business logic
594: - application notification workflows
595: - dashboard metrics
596: - notifications queries
597: 
598: Coverage needed for AI layer:
599: 
600: - pre-evaluation workflow steps (with mocked LLM responses)
601: - report generation workflow steps
602: - interview agent state transitions
603: - quota exhaustion logic
604: 
605: ---
606: 
607: ## 14. AI Architecture
608: 
609: The AI layer runs in a separate `edge/` Cloudflare Worker, triggered by authenticated HTTP calls from the main app.
610: 
611: ### Pre-Evaluation Pipeline (Cloudflare Workflow)
612: 
613: - Triggered when the main app POSTs to `/pre-evaluate` on the edge Worker
614: - Durable multi-step execution:
615:   1. Read application + job from Postgres
616:   2. Fetch resume from R2
617:   3. Extract text from resume based on file type (PDF / DOCX)
618:   4. Merge profile metadata + resume text + job context
619:   5. Call LLM for scoring
620:   6. Write result to `pre_evaluations`
621:   7. Decision layer: create interview or hold
622: - Automatic retries per step
623: - Resumes from last completed step if interrupted
624: 
625: ### Interview Layer (Cloudflare Agents SDK)
626: 
627: - One `AIChatAgent` instance per interview session (extends Durable Object)
628: - Built-in message persistence via `AIChatAgent` SQLite storage
629: - WebSocket streaming transport (token-by-token responses)
630: - System prompt injected with job requirements + resume context via Session API
631: - Two modes:
632:   - `full`: complete RoundZero interview
633:   - `quick_eval`: 2–3 clarifying questions for medium-fit candidates
634: - Interview invites expire after 48 hours via `this.schedule()` (per-interview alarm, no global cron)
635: 
636: **Agents SDK capabilities used:**
637: 
638: | Feature | How we use it | What it replaces |
639: |---|---|---|
640: | `AIChatAgent` | Interview agent class with `onChatMessage()` | Raw Durable Object + manual storage |
641: | `streamText()` | Token streaming to candidate | Full-response waiting |
642: | Tools (`tool()`) | `evaluate_answer`, `check_resume_gap`, `end_interview` | Hardcoded question limits |
643: | Session API | Structured context memory (job, candidate, evaluation notes) | Flat string concat |
644: | `this.schedule()` | Per-interview expiry alarm | Global cron polling |
645: | `this.runWorkflow()` | Trigger post-evaluation from agent | HTTP POST to endpoint |
646: | State sync | Real-time status/scores to client | Frontend polling |
647: | `this.queue()` | Background context refresh | Inline blocking fetch |
648: 
649: **Agent decision making:**
650: - The LLM decides when to end the interview via `end_interview` tool (no hardcoded 5-question limit)
651: - The agent evaluates each answer via `evaluate_answer` tool and stores running scores
652: - The agent checks claims against resume via `check_resume_gap` tool
653: - The agent triggers post-evaluation workflow directly when sufficient signal is gathered
654: 
655: ### Interview Lifecycle Manager (Agent Scheduling)
656: 
657: - Each interview schedules its own expiry via `this.schedule(48h, "expireInterview")`
658: - On expiry: agent updates status, sends notification, triggers backfill workflow
659: - No global cron needed — each interview manages its own lifecycle
660: - Agent schedules are persisted in SQLite and survive restarts
661: 
662: ### Report Generation Pipeline (Cloudflare Workflow)
663: 
664: - Triggered when interview completes (main app POSTs to `/post-evaluate`)
665: - Durable multi-step execution:
666:   1. Idempotency check (skip if report already exists)
667:   2. Read interview context + transcript from Durable Object state
668:   3. Generate report via single LLM call with structured JSON schema output
669:      - Fallback deterministic report when LLM returns non-JSON or invalid shape
670:   4. Persist report to `reports` table; update application status → `evaluated`
671:   5. Create in-app `report_ready` notification for company owner
672:   6. Send best-effort Resend email to company owner
673: 
674: ### Output Layer
675: 
676: - Report reads from Postgres
677: - Candidate ranking per job by report score
678: - Company dashboard shows evaluated + pending tabs
679: 
680: ### Key Constraint
681: 
682: - The AI layer sits on top of a complete hiring platform, not replacing unfinished basics
683: 
684: ---
685: 
686: ## 15. Near-Term Priorities
687: 
688: See `PLAN.md` for the full build plan. Current focus:
689: 
690: 1. **Interview UX polish**: finish chat auto-scroll parity, duplicate-assistant safeguards, and terminal state UI polish
691: 2. **Phase 8 wrap-up**: candidate applications list visible status labels, dedicated interview invitation cards
692: 3. **Phase 9 polish**: mobile responsive pass, pending/evaluated tabs on job applicants
693: 4. **Testing**: end-to-end smoke test of full apply → pre-eval → invite → interview → complete → report flow
694: 5. **Optional**: Better Auth migration (Phase 10), Web Interface Guidelines compliance (Phase 11)
695: 
696: ---
697: 
698: ## 16. Post-Release Hardening (Edge / AI Layer)
699: 
700: | Item | Why | Approach |
701: | --- | --- | --- |
702: | Recovery sweep for stuck applications | Fire-and-forget trigger has no retry — if edge is down, applications stay in `applied` with no pre-evaluation forever | Add a cron (CF Cron Trigger or main app scheduled task) that finds `applied` rows with no `pre_evaluations` row and re-triggers them |
703: | Quota race condition | Two concurrent workflows can over-invite for a job if capacity checks are non-atomic | Use transactional locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) on job-level capacity checks when creating interviews |
704: | LLM model adequacy | Interview chat currently uses `@cf/zai-org/glm-4.7-flash`; pre-eval/report quality can still drift by role complexity | Keep periodic score-quality checks and re-evaluate model mix if report consistency drops |
705: | Workflow failure orphans | If workflow errors after `write_pre_evaluation` but before `decide_next_step`, application is stuck in `pre_screening` | Recovery sweep covers this too — detect `pre_screening` rows older than N minutes with no interview |
706: | Edge Worker secret rotation | Shared secret is a single static value | Use a proper random secret in prod; consider HMAC request signing or CF Access Service Tokens for zero-trust |
707: 
708: ---
709: 
710: ## 17. Key Decisions
711: 
712: | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
713: | --- | --- | --- |
714: | Product layering | Platform first, AI second | Avoids using AI to mask workflow gaps |
715: | DB typing | SQLC + inference | Keeps DB layer authoritative |
716: | Resume persistence | `resume_key` | Stable storage reference |
717: | Resume delivery | Signed read URLs | Keeps resumes private |
718: | Resume upload | Direct-to-R2 signed upload | Avoids proxying file bytes through app server |
719: | Notifications | In-app notifications + Resend | Durable app record first, email as secondary delivery |
720: | Auth | Google OAuth + cookie session | Good enough for current phase |
721: | AI pipelines | Cloudflare Workflows in edge Worker | Durable multi-step execution with retries |
722: | Interview runtime | Cloudflare Agents SDK (`AIChatAgent`) in edge Worker | Stateful streaming chat with built-in message persistence |
723: | Resume text extraction | Local libraries per file type (PDF / DOCX) | LLM reads unstructured text; no external parser needed |

(End of file - total 723 lines)
</content>

21: 2. System runs lightweight pre-evaluation **asynchronously**
22: 3. If candidate looks promising **and job report quota is available**:
23:    - invite to RoundZero interview
24: 4. If medium fit **and job report quota is available**:
25:    - ask 2–3 clarifying questions first
26: 5. If low fit:
27:    - keep under review (no interview)
28: 6. If job report quota is exhausted:
29:    - remaining pending candidates stay in pipeline
30:    - candidates receive "position filled" notification
31:    - no new interviews are created
32: 7. Company receives evaluated candidates with reports
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: # Stage 1: Pre-Evaluation (Cheap + Fast)
37: 
38: ## Goal
39: 
40: Decide whether a candidate deserves deeper evaluation.
41: 
42: ## Inputs
43: 
44: - Resume
45: - Candidate profile
46: - Job description
47: - Required skills
48: - Company custom questions
49: 
50: ## Output
51: 
52: - Fit score
53: - Missing requirements
54: - Confidence
55: - Next step
56: 
57: ## Example Output
58: 
59: - Score: 78
60: - Missing: AWS experience
61: - Confidence: High
62: - Next Step: Invite to RoundZero
63: 
64: ## What It Should Check
65: 
66: - Relevant skills match
67: - Relevant experience
68: - Seniority fit
69: - Basic job alignment
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: # Stage 2: Decision Layer
74: 
75: ## Quota Check First
76: 
77: Each job has a `final_report_target` (default: 5, max: 15). The system should deliver that many final reports when enough eligible candidates exist.
78: 
79: Capacity is computed from completed reports and active interviews:
80: - `remainingReports = final_report_target - completedReports`
81: - `availableInviteSlots = remainingReports - activeInterviews(status IN pending|in_progress)`
82: 
83: ## High Match
84: 
85: → Invite to full AI interview (if quota available)
86: 
87: ## Medium Match
88: 
89: → Ask 2–3 clarifying questions first (if quota available)
90: 
91: ## Low Match
92: 
93: → Hold in `pre_screening` (no interview)
94: 
95: ## Target Reached
96: 
97: → Stop creating interviews. Remaining pending candidates stay in pipeline and receive a "position filled" notification. They are NOT auto-rejected.
98: 
99: ## Interview Expiry + Cancel
100: 
101: - Interview invites expire after 48 hours
102: - Candidates can cancel interviews if they no longer want to participate
103: - Expired or cancelled interview slots are recycled to the next best eligible candidate
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: # Agent Identity
108: 
109: The AI interviewer is named **Zero**.
110: 
111: Candidate-facing copy references Zero by name:
112: - "Zero invited you to complete an interview for this role."
113: - "Your interview with Zero is in progress."
114: - "Zero has completed the evaluation."
115: 
116: This is a product branding decision, not a model name. The underlying agent class can change; Zero is the user-facing identity.
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: # Interview Agent Implementation
121: 
122: The interview agent is implemented using the **Cloudflare Agents SDK** (`agents`, `@cloudflare/ai-chat`, `workers-ai-provider`):
123: 
124: - `AIChatAgent` class handles message history, streaming, and WebSocket transport
125: - `streamText()` from the AI SDK v5 streams tokens in real-time to the candidate
126: - `convertToModelMessages()` converts agent message history into LLM-ready format
127: - Tools allow the agent to evaluate answers, check resume gaps, and decide when to end
128: - System prompt is injected with job description, candidate summary, and pre-eval context
129: - Session state (status, scores, metadata) persisted via `this.setState()` / `this.state`
130: 
131: This replaces the previous raw Durable Object + `env.AI.run()` approach that lacked streaming, tools, and conversational memory.
132: 
133: ## Agent Tools
134: 
135: The agent has three server-side tools it can call during the conversation:
136: 
137: ### `evaluate_answer`
138: - **Input:** `{ relevance: number, depth: number, clarity: number }`
139: - **Action:** Stores running evaluation scores in agent state
140: - **When called:** After each candidate answer, the LLM self-evaluates
141: 
142: ### `check_resume_gap`
143: - **Input:** `{ claim: string }`
144: - **Action:** Queries the candidate summary to verify a specific claim
145: - **When called:** When the candidate mentions a project, skill, or company the agent wants to verify
146: 
147: ### `end_interview`
148: - **Input:** `{ reason: string }`
149: - **Action:** Sets status to `completed`, triggers post-evaluation workflow
150: - **When called:** When the LLM decides sufficient signal has been gathered (no hardcoded limit)
151: 
152: ## Agent Lifecycle
153: 
154: ### `onStart()`
155: - Ensures expiry scheduling for active sessions
156: - Schedules 48-hour expiry alarm: `this.schedule(48h, "expireInterview", undefined, { idempotent: true })`
157: 
158: ### `onChatMessage()`
159: - Streams response via `streamText()` with full message history
160: - LLM can call tools mid-conversation
161: - State syncs to client via WebSocket automatically
162: - Uses `stepCountIs(...)` stop control for bounded tool-call loops
163: 
164: ### `expireInterview()`
165: - Called by scheduled alarm after 48 hours
166: - Sets status to `expired` if not completed/cancelled
167: - Persists interview status update to Postgres
168: 
169: ### `triggerPostEvaluation()`
170: - Called by `end_interview` tool
171: - Triggers post-evaluation workflow with `this.runWorkflow("POST_EVALUATION", { interviewId })`
172: 
173: ## Session State
174: 
175: Current implementation persists interview session metadata in agent state via `this.setState()`:
176: 
177: - status (`pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `expired`)
178: - question counters (`askedQuestions`, `maxQuestions`)
179: - running evaluation aggregates
180: - timestamps (`startedAt`, `completedAt`, `cancelledAt`, `updatedAt`)
181: - normalized interview context (job/candidate/pre-eval)
182: 
183: Conversation messages are persisted by `AIChatAgent` automatically.
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: # Stage 3: Deep Evaluation
188: 
189: Only for selected candidates.
190: 
191: ## Goal
192: 
193: Measure actual hiring signal beyond resume.
194: 
195: ## What Happens
196: 
197: - Resume clarification
198: - Role-specific questions
199: - Problem solving
200: - Tradeoff / judgment questions
201: - Dynamic follow-ups
202: 
203: ## Output
204: 
205: Structured candidate report
206: 
207: ---
208: 
209: # Report Limits
210: 
211: Companies set `final_report_target` during job creation (default: 5, max: 15). This controls how many final candidate reports RoundZero will deliver for that role.
212: 
213: Why a limit:
214: - Prevents noise for companies with only 1 opening
215: - Keeps evaluation costs predictable
216: - Forces selectivity in the funnel
217: 
218: When the target is reached, the pipeline closes for new evaluations but the job may remain open. Companies still see unevaluated applicants in a pending list and can manually review or reject them.
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: # Candidate Experience
223: 
224: ## After Apply
225: 
226: ### Strong Fit
227: "Zero invited you to complete an interview for this role."
228: 
229: ### Medium Fit
230: "Zero has a few additional questions to help evaluate your fit."
231: 
232: ### Low Fit
233: "Application received and under review."
234: 
235: ### Position Filled (Quota Reached)
236: "This position has received enough evaluations. Your application is still on file and the company may review it directly."
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: # Company Experience
241: 
242: Instead of raw applicants, companies see evaluated candidates.
243: 
244: ## Candidate Card
245: 
246: - Name
247: - Score
248: - Strengths
249: - Concerns
250: - Status
251: 
252: ## Full Report
253: 
254: - Overall score
255: - Summary
256: - Technical reasoning
257: - Communication
258: - Experience relevance
259: - Strengths
260: - Risks
261: - Resume
262: - Transcript (optional)
263: 
264: ---
265: 
266: # Application Status Lifecycle (Decided)
267: 
268: > See **platform.md § 15.1** for the full decision.
269: 
270: **Decided:** Extend `applications.status` to include all 8 statuses in a single enum.
271: 
272: **Status Funnel:**
273: - `applied` → `pre_screening` → (`interview_invited` | other outcome) → `interview_in_progress` → `evaluated` → (`shortlisted` | `rejected`)
274: 
275: **Transition Rules:**
276: - Only companies can move `evaluated` → `shortlisted` or `rejected`
277: - System auto-advances through `pre_screening` → `interview_invited` → `interview_in_progress` → `evaluated`
278: - Companies can manually reject at any pre-evaluation stage
279: - When `final_report_target` is reached, system stops advancing new candidates out of `pre_screening`
280: 
281: ---
282: 
283: # Important Notes
284: 
285: ## Pre-Evaluation should NOT decide final hiring
286: 
287: It only decides:
288: 
289: "Who deserves deeper evaluation?"
290: 
291: ## Avoid keyword-only matching
292: 
293: Use semantic/contextual matching.
294: 
295: ## Keep V1 Simple
296: 
297: Build:
298: - pre-screening
299: - selective AI interviews
300: - candidate reports
301: 
302: Skip for now:
303: - voice/video
304: - multiple visible agents
305: - advanced analytics
306: - over-engineered systems
307: 
308: ---
309: 
310: # Long-Term Opportunity
311: 
312: Reusable candidate profile:
313: 
314: If a candidate completed RoundZero recently:
315: - reuse previous evaluation
316: - ask only role-specific delta questions
317: 
318: This reduces cost and improves UX.
319: 
320: ---
321: 
322: # Product Decisions (Phase 3.5 Exit Criteria)
323: 
324: > All 5 product decisions are documented in **platform.md § 15**. Refer there for full context.
325: 
326: ## Decided Decisions
327: 
328: | # | Decision | Status |
329: |---|----------|--------|
330: | 1 | Application Status Lifecycle | ✅ Extend single `applications.status` enum to all 8 statuses |
331: | 2 | Candidate-Facing Messaging | ✅ Hide pre-evaluation stages; show only 6 candidate-visible statuses |
332: | 3 | Medium-Fit Follow-Up | ✅ Use synchronous chat UI (same as full interview) with 2–3 questions |
333: | 4 | Company View Pre/Post AI | ✅ Show full pipeline; pre-eval candidates are read-only, post-eval show real scores |
334: | 5 | Pre-Evaluation Output Format | ✅ Pipeline live; real-world validation with hiring managers deferred to post-MVP |
335: | 6 | Final Report Target | ✅ `final_report_target` per job (default: 5, max: 15). Target reached → stop new evaluations, notify candidates, no auto-reject. |
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: # One-Line Summary
340: 
341: RoundZero deeply evaluates the right candidates, not every candidate.

(End of file - total 341 lines)
</content>

<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [label="yes"];
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

24: };

27:   if (typeof value !== "object" || value === null) {

30:

32:   if (!Array.isArray(record.messages)) {

parts.text:
Found and fixed the root issue.

What was happening:

- Starting interview from TanStack calls `startMyInterview` (app DB status update + edge `/internal/interviews/:id/start`).
- Edge `/start` only called `markStarted()` on the agent.
- Initial greeting (`kickoff()`) was only being called by the frontend fallback effect in `app/routes/_authenticated/interview/$interviewId.tsx`, and that can race/miss depending on message/state timing, leaving the user to type first.

What I changed:

- Updated `edge/src/shared/interview-agent-client.ts` so `markInterviewAgentStarted()` now:
  1. calls `stub.markStarted()`
  2. if started, immediately calls `stub.kickoff()`
  3. returns `{ started, greeted }`

Result:

- Greeting is now server-driven as part of the start handshake, so Zero greets immediately after Start without requiring candidate input.
- Existing safeguards still prevent duplicate greetings (`kickoff()` exits if assistant message already exists).

Validation:

- Ran `bun run check` successfully.

If you want, next I can also remove the frontend kickoff fallback in `app/routes/_authenticated/interview/$interviewId.tsx` to make this single-source and avoid any redundant kickoff attempts.

## Important notes

* **`saveMessages` is awaitable.** After it returns, the LLM has responded and the message is persisted. Use this when you control the trigger.
* **Use the function form of `saveMessages`.** `saveMessages((messages) => [...messages, newMsg])` reads the latest persisted messages at execution time, avoiding stale baselines when multiple calls queue up.
* **`persistMessages` does not trigger a response.** Use it to inject context or system messages silently.
* **`onChatResponse` is for reacting to turns you did not initiate.** Use it for user-initiated messages, auto-continuations, or any turn where you did not call `saveMessages` yourself.
* **`onChatResponse` does not nest.** When `saveMessages` is called from inside `onChatResponse`, the inner turn completes and `onChatResponse` fires again sequentially — not recursively.
* **Messages are persisted before `onChatResponse` fires.** If the Durable Object evicts during the hook, the conversation is safe in SQLite — only the hook callback is lost.
* **`waitUntilStable()` before injecting.** Always call this from schedule callbacks, webhooks, or other non-chat entry points to avoid overlapping with an in-flight stream or pending tool interaction.
* **The client sees the completed response before `onChatResponse` runs.** The server-side hook does not delay the client.
* **`messageConcurrency` does not affect `saveMessages`.** Server-driven messages always queue and execute in order.

### `messageConcurrency`

Controls how overlapping user submissions behave when a chat turn is already active or queued.

* [  JavaScript ](#tab-panel-3946)
* [  TypeScript ](#tab-panel-3947)

JavaScript

TypeScript

| Strategy                                      | Behavior                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "queue" (default)                             | Queue every submission and process in order                                                                                         |
| "latest"                                      | Keep only the latest overlapping submission; superseded submissions still persist their user messages but do not start a model turn |
| "merge"                                       | Queue overlapping submissions, then collapse their trailing user messages into one combined turn before the latest queued turn runs |
| "drop"                                        | Ignore overlapping submissions entirely                                                                                             |
| { strategy: "debounce", debounceMs?: number } | Trailing-edge latest with a quiet window (default 750ms)                                                                            |

## Think vs AIChatAgent

Both Think and [AIChatAgent](/agents/api-reference/chat-agents/) extend `Agent` and speak the same `cf_agent_chat_*` WebSocket protocol. They serve different goals.

**AIChatAgent** is a protocol adapter. You override `onChatMessage` and are responsible for calling `streamText`, wiring tools, converting messages, and returning a `Response`. AIChatAgent handles the plumbing — message persistence, streaming, abort, resume — but the LLM call is entirely your concern.

**Think** is an opinionated framework. It makes decisions for you: `getModel()` returns the model, `getSystemPrompt()` or `configureSession()` sets the prompt, `getTools()` returns tools. The default `onChatMessage` runs the complete agentic loop. You override individual pieces, not the whole pipeline.

You’re absolutely right — and CF docs point to the exact issue pattern.

What was wrong:

- Greeting was being triggered from two places:
  - frontend effect (`chat.kickoff()` when `in_progress` + no messages)
  - backend start sync (`markStarted` → `kickoff`)
- With reconnect/hydration timing, both paths can race and generate multiple “first” assistant turns.
- CF guidance says for non-chat entry points, use `waitUntilStable()` and avoid overlapping injections. Also, server-driven injections should be single-owner.

What I changed:

- Removed frontend kickoff trigger entirely from `app/routes/_authenticated/interview/$interviewId.tsx` (no more `useEffect` kickoff path).
- Made agent kickoff idempotent in `edge/src/agents/interview-agent.ts`:
  - added `kickoffGeneratedAt` in agent state
  - early return if kickoff already happened
  - if assistant message already exists, mark kickoff as consumed and return
  - call `waitUntilStable({ timeout: 10_000 })` before injecting greeting (CF-recommended pattern for non-chat triggers)

Why this should stop duplicates:

- Single source of truth: only backend start flow triggers kickoff.
- Agent-level guard prevents repeated greetings across reconnects/retries/races.
- Stability wait reduces overlaps with inflight persistence/stream state.

Also checked:

- `bun run check` passes.

If you still see duplicates after this, next I’ll add a very strict content/idempotency guard (e.g. `metadata.kickoffId`) and log request IDs in kickoff so we can trace exactly which caller path is still firing.

Nice catch — agreed, it felt dead.

I added immediate button feedback on the interview action:

- In `app/routes/_authenticated/interview/$interviewId.tsx`, the primary button now shows:
  - `Starting...` while `startMutation.isPending`

- It already had `disabled` during pending, so now users get both visual lock + explicit progress text.

`bun run check` passes.

If you want, next I can add a tiny inline status line above chat (“Starting interview…”) for extra clarity during slower edge roundtrips.

parts.text:
You’re not missing anything — that was a real inconsistency.

You were correct:

- Manual submit path (`completeMyInterview`) sets application status to `evaluated`.
- Agent-ended path (`end_interview` -> `POST_EVALUATION`) generated the report but never updated application status, so cards stayed `Under Review`.

I fixed it in `edge/src/workflows/post-evaluation.ts`:

- After report persistence, workflow now sets application status to `evaluated`.
- Also added reconciliation for idempotent re-runs:
  - if report already exists, workflow still updates application status to `evaluated` before returning.

So now both completion paths converge on the same final application state.

Validation:

- `bun run check` passes.

Nice catch — this was exactly the kind of cross-path drift that’s easy to miss.

interesting. from a product perspective is that an expected behavior? I mean what does evaluated mean here? does it mean the candidate's flow has completed and the company is yet to respond or does it mean the company has selected that candidate? I dont think its the latter right?

Yep, it’s not the latter.

`evaluated` in your current model means:

- the automated evaluation flow is complete (interview done + report available)
- the application is now waiting on company decision
- next company actions are typically `shortlisted` or `rejected`

So product-wise it’s “evaluation completed, decision pending,” not “candidate selected.”

If you want clearer UX language, you could keep the DB status as `evaluated` but map it in UI copy to something like:

1. `Reviewed` (short)
2. `Evaluation complete` (explicit)
3. `Awaiting company decision` (most clear)

yeah do 3. the candidate should clearly know what these mean[Image 1] but im afraid it will also duplicate messaging? since this application detail page already says interview completed and the company will review your evaluation? is it good enough or?

You’re thinking about this exactly right.  
If you apply “Awaiting company decision” everywhere, it can feel repetitive in detail view.

Best UX split:

- **List / card badge (compact):** `Awaiting company decision`
- **Detail status badge:** `Awaiting company decision`
- **Detail helper text (keep richer context):** keep the current longer sentence (or tighten slightly), e.g.  
  `Your interview is complete. The company is now reviewing your evaluation and will decide next steps.`

So it’s not duplicate messaging, it’s layered messaging:
- short label = state
- body copy = what happens next

I’d keep both, just make sure they’re not saying the exact same sentence verbatim.  
If you want, I can now update the status label mappings in the candidate-facing surfaces to this exact wording while preserving the existing detailed explainer text.

You’re right — I checked, and this gap is real.

- Company “invite to interview” from pending/applicant review goes through `updateApplicationStatus` in `app/features/applications/server/functions.ts:129`, which calls `updateApplicationStatusWorkflow` in `app/features/applications/services/workflows.ts:106`.
- That workflow only:
  - validates transition,
  - updates `applications.status`,
  - sends generic `application_status_changed` notification (`app/features/applications/services/workflows.ts:148`).
- It does **not** create an `interviews` row, does **not** initialize `InterviewAgent`, and does **not** send the structured `interview_invited` notification payload with `interviewId` + `expiresAt`.

By contrast, pre-eval invite path in `edge/src/workflows/pre-evaluation.ts:543` does the full flow correctly:
- `createInterview(...)`
- `initializeInterviewAgent(...)`
- `updateApplicationStatus(..., "interview_invited")`
- create `interview_invited` notification (`edge/src/workflows/pre-evaluation.ts:590`)

So your diagnosis is correct: manual company invite currently updates DB status but does not actually provision an interview session/agent invite.
we should fix it then? then the whole loop will be completed even for pending candidates? or will it introduce new bugs or something?

Yes — we should fix it. This is a real product gap, and closing it completes the loop for pending/hold candidates.

- Right now manual company invite only changes `applications.status` via `updateApplicationStatusWorkflow` and sends a generic status notification.
- It does **not** provision the actual interview session (`interviews` row + agent init), so candidate can look “invited” without a real interview backing it.
- Pre-eval invite path already has the correct full flow; we should mirror that behavior for manual invites.

Will this introduce bugs? It can be done safely if we make it idempotent:

- Check `getInterviewByApplicationId` first; if exists, reuse it (don’t create duplicates).
- Only initialize agent when interview is newly created.
- Send proper `interview_invited` notification payload (`interviewId`, `expiresAt`, `type`), not just generic status changed.
- Keep existing transition validation/authorization as-is.

So: **yes, fix it; low risk with proper idempotency guards**.  
If you want, I’ll implement this now in the workflow path so manual “invite to interview” behaves exactly like system-generated invite.
yes

Implemented — the pending/manual invite path now provisions a real interview invite instead of only flipping application status.

What I changed in `app/features/applications/services/workflows.ts`:

- On transition to `interview_invited`, workflow now:
  - checks for an existing interview via `getInterviewByApplicationId(...)`
  - creates one if missing via `createInterview(...)` with:
    - `status: "pending"`
    - `type: "full"` when latest pre-eval `next_step` is `interview_invited`, else `quick_eval`
    - `metadata.expiresAt` (+ `preEvaluationScore` if available)
- Sends the proper `interview_invited` notification payload (`applicationId`, `interviewId`, `jobId`, `jobTitle`, `interviewType`, `expiresAt`) and email delivery path.
- Returns early for this branch so it does **not** also send generic `application_status_changed`.

Validation:

- Ran `bun run check` successfully.

What this means behavior-wise:

- Yes, this closes the loop for pending/hold candidates promoted manually by a company.
- Candidate now gets a concrete interview session and invite notification tied to an actual `interviewId`.
- It is idempotent around duplicate creation (reuses existing interview if one already exists).
